description: Uzun süreli uzay görevlerinde astronotlar radyasyon, izolasyon ve değişen yer çekimi nedeniyle çeşitli sağlık riskleriyle karşılaşır. Görevimiz; sağlık göstergelerini toplayarak astronotların kendi durumlarını değerlendirmelerini ve gerekli önlemleri almalarını sağlayan bir sağlık izleme yazılımı geliştirmektir.
summary: ASTRO-TWIN is an autonomous 3D health digital twin for astronauts on long missions to the Moon and Mars. On a Mars transit, a message to Earth can take up to 22 minutes each way, so the crew cannot wait for a flight surgeon on the ground. ASTRO-TWIN puts one on board. A low-cost ESP32 wearable streams surface EMG, pulse, SpO2 and temperature at 20 Hz into a browser app, where a 3D anatomical twin shows five body systems as nominal, caution or critical. The five systems follow NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight: altered gravity, fluid shift and closed cabin, isolation and confinement, hostile environment, and radiation and distance from Earth. A triage engine turns the readings into a readiness score, an EVA go/no-go decision and a concrete countermeasure, and switches to an autonomous onboard protocol when Earth is too far away. An offline voice AI flight surgeon answers the crew's questions about their own data. Every threshold is grounded in NASA data, including Curiosity MSL-RAD radiation measurements, NASA-STD-3001, the NASA Twins Study, NASA OSDR, Standard Measures, CIPHER and NASA-TLX. ASTRO-TWIN matters because crews heading to Mars will have to detect and treat health problems themselves.
details:
What it does

ASTRO-TWIN is an autonomous health monitoring and decision-support system for astronauts on long missions. It combines a wearable sensor node, a 3D anatomical digital twin of the crew member and an onboard triage engine. It watches five body systems in real time, flags problems early and tells the crew what to do, even when Earth is up to 22 minutes away on a Mars transit.

How it works

1. Sense: An ESP32 node reads a surface EMG sensor (muscle activation and fatigue) and a MAX30100 optical sensor (pulse and SpO2), with optional MLX90614 infrared temperature. It streams a JSON telemetry frame at 20 Hz over USB (Web Serial API) or through a Raspberry Pi 3 edge bridge. The crew also logs blood pressure, glucose, sleep, mood and the six-subscale NASA-TLX workload score.

2. Model: A Three.js 3D twin maps the data to five body systems that follow NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight. Each system is shown as nominal (green), caution (amber) or critical (red). A mission timeline (Sol 1 to 1,000) projects cumulative radiation dose, bone loss and SANS risk for ISS, lunar and Mars missions.

3. Decide: A rule-based triage engine checks each system against thresholds from NASA standards and returns a crew readiness score, an EVA go/no-go decision and an escalation level: crew self-care, flight-surgeon alert, or an autonomous onboard protocol when the mission is too far from Earth.

4. Act: For each hazard it gives a concrete countermeasure, for example cutting resistive exercise load by 20%, stopping exertion and checking cabin O2/CO2, or enforcing a sleep block. The ASTRO-AI voice flight surgeon answers questions about the live data by voice or text. It works offline; a cloud model is optional.

How we used NASA data

- Curiosity MSL-RAD measurements (NTRS 20250004252): daily radiation dose per environment, up to 1.84 mSv/day in Mars transit, and cumulative dose against the 600 mSv career limit.

- NASA-STD-3001 and the OCHMO ECLSS technical brief: cabin CO2 limit of 3.0 mmHg and the CO2/O2 metabolic model.

- HRP 5 Hazards, HRP risks and the Moon to Mars review: the five body systems and a risk heatmap from ISS to Mars.

- NASA Twins Study: evidence cards on telomeres, gene expression, vascular changes and SANS.

- NASA OSDR: the EMG muscle fatigue and atrophy model (median frequency shift).

- Spaceflight Standard Measures and CIPHER: a 6-axis radar comparing live data with Earth baseline and long-flight reference.

- NASA-TLX and the HRP sleep evidence report (NTRS 20150016964): workload score and about 6 h real sleep vs 8.5 h planned.

- NASA SRAG: South Atlantic Anomaly map with the ISS 51.6-degree ground track.

Benefits and intended impact

- Five body systems in one view with one readiness score, so problems are seen early instead of at the next scheduled check.

- Decisions on board in seconds instead of waiting up to 44 minutes for a reply from Earth.

- Built from low-cost, off-the-shelf parts and a single browser page, so analog missions, schools and remote teams on Earth (polar stations, ships, rural clinics) can build and test it.

Our goal: every crew carries its own flight surgeon.

Tools, languages and hardware

HTML, CSS and JavaScript; Three.js (3D), D3.js and TopoJSON (maps), Tailwind CSS; Web Serial API and Web Speech API; Arduino C++ firmware for the ESP32; Raspberry Pi 3 as an edge node. Hardware: ESP32, surface EMG sensor with electrodes, MAX30100 pulse oximeter, optional MLX90614 infrared thermometer, and a UNI-T oscilloscope for signal validation.

Creativity

ASTRO-TWIN turns abstract spaceflight risk data into a body the crew can see: a live 3D twin whose organs change color, whose arm flexes with the real EMG signal and whose heart beats at the real pulse. It links real hardware, NASA datasets and an offline AI doctor in one page, with gamified health quests to keep the crew engaged.

What we considered

- Communication delay: the system must work without Earth, so all core logic runs locally.

- False alarms: thresholds are tuned so that finger movement on the low-cost optical sensor does not trigger critical alarms.

- Trust: every threshold is traceable to a NASA source shown in the app.

- Accessibility: Turkish/English interface, voice output, and a text label next to every color status.

- Safety: ASTRO-TWIN is a research and education prototype, not a certified medical device.
